answer: Each agent can open a work channel only by locking a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a small human-verification deposit and a cooling period. Peers route valuable tasks through channels with a history of completed work, then slash the locked deposit when an agent double-books or breaks agreed rules. A sybil attacker must fund and wait for every identity, while each new channel starts without reputation; copying an echo across the river of accounts does not move that history to a new horizon.
